\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Sign encoding via the Boolean real embedding]
\lean{FABL.realSignEncodedFunction_eq_one_sub_two_booleanRealEmbedding}
\label{FABL.realSignEncodedFunction_eq_one_sub_two_booleanRealEmbedding}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.signEncode, FABL.signEncodedFunction}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$ be a Boolean function, and define its real embedding
to be $1$ where $f(x)=1$ and $0$ otherwise. Its real sign encoding is the function
$x\mapsto 1-2$ times this real embedding.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of the sign encoding]
\lean{FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff_realSignEncodedFunction_eq_neg_two_mul}
\label{FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff_realSignEncodedFunction_eq_neg_two_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.expect_indexedMonomial_mul, FABL.indexedFourierCoeff, FABL.indexedMonomial, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction_eq_one_sub_two_booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.signRestriction_apply}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, let $A$ be a nonempty
subset of $J$, and fix signs on the coordinates outside $J$. On the resulting restricted
sign cube, the Fourier coefficient indexed by $A$ of the real-valued sign encoding
$x\mapsto(-1)^{f(x)}$ is $-2$ times the coefficient indexed by $A$ of the indicator
function of the event $f(x)=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Even scaling of restricted Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.even_scaled_restrictionFourierCoeff_of_isBent}
\label{FABL.even_scaled_restrictionFourierCoeff_of_isBent}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsBent, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.f₂CubeEquivFinset, FABL.f₂Support, FABL.indexedMonomial, FABL.indexedMonomial_sq, FABL.liftFixedFrequency, FABL.liftFreeFrequency, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff_eq_sum, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff_binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the
$n$-dimensional binary cube, and suppose every Fourier coefficient of $f$ has absolute
value $2^{-\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$. Let $J$ be a set of coordinates whose complement is
nonempty, let $A\subseteq J$, and fix signs on the coordinates outside $J$. Then the
Fourier coefficient indexed by $A$ of the restriction of the corresponding sign-cube
function, with those outside signs fixed, is $q\,2^{-\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ for some even
integer $q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Granularity from bentness]
\lean{FABL.isVectorFourierGranular_booleanRealEmbedding_of_isBent}
\label{FABL.isVectorFourierGranular_booleanRealEmbedding_of_isBent}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.IsBent, FABL.IsVectorFourierGranular, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.fourierCoeff_one_sub_div_two, FABL.f₂Support, FABL.isVectorFourierGranular_iff, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction_eq_one_sub_two_booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff_binaryFunctionOnSignCube}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional cube over $bf_2$ to $bf_2$. If the real
sign encoding of $f$ is bent, meaning that every vector Fourier coefficient has absolute
value $2^{-\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, then the function that takes value $1$ where $f=1$ and
$0$ elsewhere is vector Fourier granular with granularity $2^{-(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1)}$:
each of its Fourier coefficients on the sign cube is an integer multiple of this number.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Algebraic degree bound for bent functions]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_le_half_of_isBent}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p165-b003}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_le_half_of_isBent}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.IsBent, FABL.even_scaled_restrictionFourierCoeff_of_isBent, FABL.exists_odd_restrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.exists_top_anfCoeff, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_le_of_isVectorFourierGranular_booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_zero, FABL.isVectorFourierGranular_booleanRealEmbedding_of_isBent, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff_realSignEncodedFunction_eq_neg_two_mul, FABL.zeroFixedSign}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be an even natural number with $2<n$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ be a
Boolean function. If the real-valued function obtained by encoding $f(x)$ as
$(-1)^{f(x)}$ is bent—that is, every Fourier coefficient indexed by a vector in the
binary cube has absolute value $(2^{n/2})^{-1}$—then the algebraic degree of $f$ is at
most $n/2$.
\end{theorem}
